competitors.title: LlamaIndex Docs: Building an Agent
key_points: LlamaIndex is the leading framework for building LLM-powered agents over your data with agents and workflows
Agents are LLM-powered knowledge assistants that use tools to perform tasks like research, data extraction, and more
Workflows are multi-step processes combining agents, data connectors, and tools for complex tasks with reflection and error-correction
LlamaParse provides agentic OCR and document parsing for 130+ formats
LlamaExtract enables structured data extraction from documents with human-defined or inferred schemas
LlamaCloud provides managed indexing/retrieval pipelines with automatic document processing and syncing

competitors.title: LlamaIndex Docs: Multi-Agent Patterns
key_points: Three multi-agent patterns: AgentWorkflow (linear swarm), Orchestrator agent (sub-agents as tools), Custom planner (DIY prompting + parsing)
AgentWorkflow manages hand-offs between specialist agents automatically with built-in streaming and events
Orchestrator pattern exposes each sub-agent's run method as a tool to a top-level orchestrator for custom control flow
Custom planner pattern gives ultimate flexibility with XML/JSON plan formats and imperative execution
Multi-agent report generation example: ResearchAgent → WriteAgent → ReviewAgent with state management across handoffs
Pattern choice depends on lines of code vs flexibility tradeoff: AgentWorkflow (fewest), Orchestrator (medium), Custom planner (most)

angles: Long-horizon document agents solve the 'document amnesia' problem: standard RAG loses context across multi-step document processing pipelines — LlamaIndex workflows maintain state across parsing, extraction, indexing, and querying stages

The three-tier multi-agent architecture: use AgentWorkflow for simple document pipelines, Orchestrator for controlled document processing with human-in-the-loop, and Custom Planner for complex document workflows with branching logic

Document agent pipeline as a production stack: LlamaParse (ingestion) → LlamaExtract (structured data) → LlamaCloud Index (retrieval) → Agent (query/reasoning) — each stage needs checkpointing for long-horizon reliability
Parallel document processing with fan-out agents: split large document sets into subcategories, process with parallel sub-agents, then merge results — critical for enterprise-scale document workflows

Long-horizon failure modes in document agents: context drift across multi-page documents, false completion on partial extraction, unbounded exploration of document sections, and destructive tool use on source files

Cost optimization for long-horizon document agents: token budgets per document, step limits per pipeline, and model routing (cheap models for parsing/classification, frontier models for extraction/reasoning)

The 2026 document agent landscape: LlamaIndex dominates open-source document agents, but LangGraph, CrewAI, and OpenAI Agents SDK each offer different document workflow patterns with different state management approaches
